entries.description_source_en: Their coloring changes according to the seasons and can be slightly affected by the temperature and humidity as well.
entries.fact_source_en: The color and scent of their fur changes to match the mountain grass. When they sense hostility, they hide in the grass.

entries.description_source_en: They migrate according to the seasons, so some people call Sawsbuck the harbingers of spring.
entries.fact_source_en: The plants growing on its horns change according to the season. The leaders of the herd possess magnificent horns.

entries.description_source_en: As Emolga flutters through the air, it crackles with electricity. This Pokémon is cute, but it can cause a lot of trouble.
entries.fact_source_en: They store up electricity to fly through the air. When thunder cracks at night, sometimes there are almost enough of them to blot out the sky.

entries.description_source_en: Its strange physiology reacts to electrical energy in interesting ways. The presence of a Shelmet will cause this Pokémon to evolve.
entries.fact_source_en: It spits a liquid from its mouth to melt through Shelmet’s shell. Karrablast doesn’t eat the shell— it eats only the contents.

entries.description_source_en: They use shells they’ve stolen from Shelmet to arm and protect themselves. They’re very popular Pokémon in the Galar region.
entries.fact_source_en: It charges its enemies, lances at the ready. An image of one of its duels is captured in a famous painting of Escavalier clashing with Sirfetch’d.

entries.description_source_en: No one knows what the Poké Ball–like pattern on Foongus means or why Foongus has it.
entries.fact_source_en: The spores released from this Pokémon’s hands are highly poisonous, but when thoroughly dried, the spores can be used as stomach medicine.

entries.description_source_en: This Pokémon puffs poisonous spores at its foes. If the spores aren’t washed off quickly, they’ll grow into mushrooms wherever they land.
entries.fact_source_en: Amoonguss generally doesn’t move much. It tends to stand still near Poké Balls that have been dropped on the ground.

entries.description_source_en: It envelops its prey in its veillike arms and draws it down to the deeps, five miles below the ocean’s surface.
entries.fact_source_en: Using the invisible poison spikes on its veillike arms and legs, it paralyzes its enemies and causes them to drown.

entries.description_source_en: Most of this Pokémon’s body composition is identical to sea water. It makes sunken ships its lair.
entries.fact_source_en: Whenever a full moon hangs in the night sky, schools of Jellicent gather near the surface of the sea, waiting for their prey to appear.

entries.description_source_en: Fishermen take them along on long voyages, because if you have an Alomomola with you, there’ll be no need for a doctor or medicine.
entries.fact_source_en: The reason it helps Pokémon in a weakened condition is that any Pokémon coming after them may also attack Alomomola.

entries.description_source_en: Joltik can be found clinging to other Pokémon. It’s soaking up static electricity because it can’t produce a charge on its own.
entries.fact_source_en: Joltik latch on to other Pokémon and suck out static electricity. They’re often found sticking to Yamper’s hindquarters.

entries.description_source_en: It launches electrified fur from its abdomen as its means of attack. Opponents hit by the fur could be in for three full days and nights of paralysis.
entries.fact_source_en: It lays traps of electrified threads near the nests of bird Pokémon, aiming to snare chicks that are not yet good at flying.

entries.description_source_en: It defends itself by launching spikes, but its aim isn’t very good at first. Only after a lot of practice will it improve.
entries.fact_source_en: Mossy caves are their preferred dwellings. Enzymes contained in mosses help Ferroseed’s spikes grow big and strong.

entries.description_source_en: This Pokémon scrapes its spikes across rocks, and then uses the tips of its feelers to absorb the nutrients it finds within the stone.
entries.fact_source_en: Its spikes are harder than steel. This Pokémon crawls across rock walls by stabbing the spikes on its feelers into the stone.

entries.description_source_en: The two minigears that compose this Pokémon are closer than twins. They mesh well only with each other.
entries.fact_source_en: The two minigears that mesh together are predetermined. Each will rebound from other minigears without meshing.

entries.description_source_en: When Klang goes all out, the minigear links up perfectly with the outer part of the big gear, and this Pokémon’s rotation speed increases sharply.
entries.fact_source_en: Many companies in the Galar region choose Klang as their logo. This Pokémon is considered the symbol of industrial technology.

entries.description_source_en: From its spikes, it launches powerful blasts of electricity. Its red core contains an enormous amount of energy.
entries.fact_source_en: The minigear spins at high speed. Then the energy from the red core charges the minigear to make it ready to fire.

entries.description_source_en: One alone can emit only a trickle of electricity, so a group of them gathers to unleash a powerful electric shock.
entries.fact_source_en: These Pokémon move in schools. They have an electricity-generating organ, so they discharge electricity if in danger.

entries.description_source_en: It wraps itself around its prey and paralyzes it with electricity from the round spots on its sides. Then it chomps.
entries.fact_source_en: They coil around foes and shock them with electricity-generating organs that seem simply to be circular patterns.

entries.description_source_en: It latches on to prey with its sucker mouth, sinking in its fangs and shocking the prey with powerful electricity.
entries.fact_source_en: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.

entries.description_source_en: If this Pokémon stands near a TV, strange scenery will appear on the screen. That scenery is said to be from its home.
entries.fact_source_en: It controls tremendous psychic power. Most reports of alien sightings are actually just people mistaking Elgyem for an alien.

entries.description_source_en: Whenever a Beheeyem visits a farm, a Dubwool mysteriously disappears.
entries.fact_source_en: It has strong psychic powers. Using its fingers that flash three different colors, it controls its opponents and rewrites their memories.

entries.description_source_en: The flame on its head keeps its body slightly warm. This Pokémon takes lost children by the hand to guide them to the spirit world.
entries.fact_source_en: Litwick shines a light that absorbs the life energy of people and Pokémon, which becomes the fuel that it burns.

entries.description_source_en: This Pokémon appears just before someone passes away, so it’s feared as an emissary of death.
entries.fact_source_en: It lurks in cities, pretending to be a lamp. Once it finds someone whose death is near, it will trail quietly after them.

entries.description_source_en: This Pokémon haunts dilapidated mansions. It sways its arms to hypnotize opponents with the ominous dancing of its flames.
entries.fact_source_en: It absorbs a spirit, which it then burns. By waving the flames on its arms, it puts its foes into a hypnotic trance.
